newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA IN $50 MLN CHINA GSM EXPANSION DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA IN $50 MLN CHINA GSM EXPANSION DEAL.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy said in a statement on Wednesday it had signed a deal to expand a GSM network in Bejing.
"The deliveries will begin in February and the value of the agreement is close to $50 million," it said.
The GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) network's capacity would increase to 550,000 subscribers, Nokia said, but gave no comparison.
Deliveries would include Nokia's DX 200 mobile switching centres, base station controllers, base stations and home location registers, it said.

"Nokia will supply to Beijing the full network subsystem and also a major part of the base station sub-system," it said, adding that its short message service (SMS) centre would support messages written in Chinese characters.
"The future top-end Nokia GSM phones sold in China will have Chinese SMS as a standard feature," Nokia said.
